newsitem.title: CANADA: Bema stock weakens on exploration data.
newsitem.headline: Bema stock weakens on exploration data.

text.p: Bema Gold Corp shares fell Thursday after the company released exploration results from its Cerro Casale gold property in Chile that disappointed investors, analysts said.

Bema shares were down 0.65 at 11.40 in Toronto after bottoming at 11.10. They were off 1/2 at 8-3/8 on the American Stock Exchange. Analysts said investor expectations had soared in anticipation of further good news from Bema but the announcement Thursday did not bear out those high hopes. "The grades were rather mediocre, much lower than they previously announced," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Added another analyst, who also did not want to be identified: "The market was anticipating better results...People were expecting something more."
But analysts said the new data did not detract from previously promising data at the property in northern Chile and emphasized that exploration remains in its early stages.
Bema owns 49 percent of Cerro Casale while Arizona Star Resource Corp, in which Bema is a major shareholder, owns 51 percent. Arizona Star stock lost 0.95 to 14.40 in Vancouver.

The two companies released results from two drill holes. Among the results for various intervals, they said hole 30 had a gold grade of 0.55 grams per tonne over a length of 251 meters. Hole 29 had a grade of 0.38 grams per tonne over 250 meters.
They said hole 30 "indicates a substantial increase in the width of the main porphyry zone."
